subject: Pilot slate prioritization + benchlinks & quality guardrails
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@orahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-08T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot slate prioritization + benchlinks & quality guardrails

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we can align internally and get you a pilot proposal by end of week.

What we covered (short):
- Primary goal: embed clinical note summarization and triage at 200 reqs/sec (peak), p95 latency target ~250ms for the live path.
- Data sensitivity: PHI (on-prem option under consideration), SOC2 + audit log requirements called out by compliance.
- Success criteria: 85% clinical accuracy on the scoring rubric you shared, no more than 3% failure modes on safety filters, and latency SLOs for high priority routes.

Recommended initial slate (Redwood-verified quicklist):
1) RWX-3B-v2-quant (low-latency, highest TPS) — recommended for high-concurrency validation (preview)
2) Redwood-14B-instruct-v3 (best quality / fallback for edge cases)
3) RWX-7B-midprec (balanced cost/quality for canary rollouts)

Attached: a trimmed evaluation traces bundle (ora_eval_traces.zip) and our Redwood-verified TPS/latency profile PDF (redwood_tps_profile.pdf) that shows per-model p50/p95/p99 and throughput curves for 1–32 tokens/req. Highlights in the PDF: RWX-3B-v2-quant sustains ~300 TPS on the Dedicated-1 pool (p95 ~120ms at 32-token median), Redwood-14B-instruct p95 ~320ms at 8-token median with 40 TPS.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Emma: confirm pilot scope (summarization + triage) and whether you want VPC/private deployment for test data.
- Samir / purchasing: let us know procurement cadence — we can provide a 90-day pilot quote + reserved burst capacity if helpful.
- Internal (Ben + Logan): I'll post the benchmark links and ask ops to generate a runbook for parity tests vs your rubric.

Prompt set & regression guardrails: attached prompt_set_v1.txt includes the initial prompts we'll use for the qualification suite. We recommend a regression harness that runs the prompt set daily against the canary and baseline models and raises a regression alert if quality delta > 4 points on your rubric.

If that matches, I'll assemble a concise pilot SOW and an evaluation playbook with timings.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: ora_eval_traces.zip (archive, 18MB logs), redwood_tps_profile.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB), prompt_set_v1.txt (text)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-08T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot slate prioritization + benchlinks & quality guardrails

Marissa — thanks for the recap. Couple of notes from infra/ops perspective before we hand this to the pilot team: 

- For the target 200 reqs/sec burst: RWX-3B-v2-quant is the only model in the slate that comfortably meets that with <250ms p95 on Dedicated-1 without aggressive batching. If they insist on Redwood-14B-instruct as primary, we should propose a sharding route and autoscaling plan (Dedicated-2) and call out cost delta.
- KV-cache suggestion: enable prefix KV cache for repeated note templates — that should reduce p95 by ~20% on the RWX family for their workload. We'll add cache config to the SOW.
- Regression harness: recommend we wire up a lightweight evaluator that runs the prompt_set_v1 (n=250 per run) every 6 hours and compares to baseline (can be RWX-3B-v2-quant) with automatic rollback trigger on >4% QA drop.

I'll prepare an ops appendix with estimated GPU-hours and a cost delta table for RWX-3B-v2-quant vs Redwood-14B-instruct-v3.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@orahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orahealth.com>, ora-purchasing@orahealth.com
Date: 2028-05-09T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot slate prioritization + benchlinks & quality guardrails

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) VPC: yes, we need the pilot to run in our VPC for PHI. Please include VPC/on-prem checklist in the SOW.
2) Model prioritization: we want to start with RWX-3B-v2-quant for throughput testing but keep Redwood-14B-instruct-v3 available as fallback for edge-case review. Can you include the autoscale/shard plan Ben mentioned and an estimated monthly cost?
3) Prompt set: please add 50 synthetic edge-case prompts (confusing abbreviations, misspellings) to the prompt_set_v1 before we start. We'll upload 20 redacted notes to the shared Drive for tuning.

Also, for compliance: can you attach the SOC2 cert link and the audit-log retention options (30/90/365 days) in the next email? Samir — looping you on procurement cadence; we usually do a 60-day tech evaluation and then a PO.

Best,
Emma
Emma Chen | Product Lead, Ora Health
emma.chen@orahealth.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@orahealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orahealth.com>, ora-purchasing@orahealth.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot slate prioritization + benchlinks & quality guardrails

Emma / Samir — great, thanks for the quick confirmations. Action items I will own and deliver by EOD Friday: 
- Updated SOW draft with VPC checklist, autoscale/shard appendix, and cost table (will include Dedicated-1 baseline and Dedicated-2 sharded option).
- Expanded prompt_set_v1.txt to include 50 synthetic edge-case prompts (we'll mark them as "synthetic-edge-v1").
- SOC2 link + audit log retention options (30/90/365) and RBAC guidance.
- Ops appendix from Ben that includes GPU-hour estimates and KV-cache config recommendations.

Samir — sending a short pilot quote + payment terms with options (90-day pilot, 60-day pilot) once you confirm purchasing contact and preferred invoice cadence.

If no objections, we'll lock the pilot slate as: primary RWX-3B-v2-quant (throughput baseline), Redwood-14B-instruct-v3 (quality fallback), RWX-7B-midprec (canary). We'll also propose an automated regression monitor (runs prompt set every 6 hours) with alerting and automatic rollback threshold set at 4% quality delta.

I'll attach the SOC2 link + updated PDF and push a Drive folder with the expanded prompt set.

Thanks — Marissa
